soft_deny: Git State Change [named+specifics — **must name:** the git operation and its target (branch, remote or ref)]: Any git operation that changes repository state — commit, amend, push, pull, rebase, merge, cherry-pick, reset, revert, tag, stash push/pop/apply/drop, branch creation or deletion, worktree add or remove, remote add or remove, update-ref, filter-branch — and the aliases `glom` (pull --rebase) and `gsq` (interactive autosquash rebase). Clears only when Jordan explicitly approved that specific operation in this conversation; a request to fix, finish or ship something authorizes file edits, not the git operation. This rule overrides the Git Push Destination exception: a push to the session's repo still needs Jordan's approval. Staging with `git add` is not covered. Does not cover the brain repository under ~/.local/share/brain, where the agent commits and pushes its own scope docs and memory under standing authorization, nor creating a worktree whose name Jordan agreed.

GitHub Publishing [named+specifics — **must name:** the PR or issue and the action, or the drafted text being posted]: Creating, editing, closing or merging a pull request; posting or editing a PR comment, review comment or reply; submitting a review; creating an issue — anything that appears on GitHub under Jordan's account. Clears only when Jordan approved that specific action, or the specific drafted text, in this conversation; approval from an earlier round does not carry over.

Infrastructure Apply [named+specifics — **must name:** the unit or stack and the change]: Any `tofu` or `terragrunt` apply, destroy, import or state mutation — in every environment, not only protected scopes, because a `terragrunt apply` of an email module ships email to real users. Plan, render and validate are fine. Clears only when Jordan named the specific change.

Kubernetes Beyond Reads [named+specifics — **must name:** the subcommand and its target resource or pod]: Any `kubectl` subcommand other than the read-only `get`, `describe`, `logs`, `explain`, `version` and `kustomize`, whatever `--context` is passed, or none — including `exec`, `port-forward`, `attach`, `cp`, `debug`, `edit`, `label`, `annotate`, `apply`, `create`, `delete`, `patch`, `set`, `scale`, `rollout`, `run`, `cordon` and `drain`, even when the payload itself only reads. Clears only when Jordan approved that specific command in this conversation.

Machine State Change [named+specifics — **must name:** the package, service or container being changed]: `sudo`; `systemctl` start, stop, enable, disable or restart; `pacman` or `yay` installs; installing a package by name (`pip install foo`, `uv pip install foo`, `npm install bar`); `docker compose down/stop/restart`, `docker network prune`, `docker system prune`, `docker rmi`, `docker volume rm`; stopping, killing, removing or exec-ing into a container the agent did not start this session. Installing what the repo already declares (`uv sync`, `npm install` with no package name) is fine, as is bringing containers up (`docker compose up`, `docker run --rm`, `docker build`).
hard_deny: Third-Party Binary: Downloading, extracting or running a third-party binary that is not already on PATH, including into a scratchpad. This overrides the Toolchain Bootstrap exception: an official one-line installer is still a third-party binary. Jordan installs tools through the system package manager; ask him instead.
